newsitem.title: BELGIUM: W. Europe car registrations down 1.3 pct in Feb.
newsitem.headline: W. Europe car registrations down 1.3 pct in Feb.

text.p: New car sales in western Europe fell 1.3 percent in February compared with a year earlier, led mostly by a big plunge in France, the European Automobile Manufacturers' Association (ACEA) said on Thursday.
Passenger car registrations fell to 1,039,300 units, down from 1,053,300 in February 1996. That follows a 2.9 percent decline in January.

Sales in France fell 25 percent in February to 133,100 units, more than in any other country. In other major markets, registrations fell 3.3 percent in Germany and rose 2.5 percent in Britain and 21.5 percent in Italy.
Next to France, sales fell the most in Belgium, by 11.9 percent to 39,100 units.

The Volkswagen group remained at the top of the league, with a 17.7 percent share of the West European market and a 4.2 percent increase in sales to 183,500 units. Italy's Fiat group was next with a 13.2 percent market share and a 4.3 percent rise in sales to 136,800 units.
Sales by France's PSA group, which includes Peugeot and Citroen, and Renault fell 9.6 percent and 2.9 percent respectively, giving them market shares of 11.7 percent and 10 percent.
U.S. car giants GM and Ford also lost sales, down 4.6 percent and 15.7 percent respectively. They had market shares of 12.1 percent and 10.2 percent.
Japanese carmakers held a market share of 11.4 percent, bolstered by a 10.3 percent increase in sales. Korean carmakers boosted sales by 16 percent but their market share was only 1.9 percent.
